name: Core Business Logic - Auto-Distribution Engine
one_line_goal: Implement the income-splitting, ceiling and redirect engine as a pure function that provably never loses or invents a single minor unit.
objective: Transcribe docs/ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md into a UI-independent, I/O-free, deterministic engine with exhaustive unit tests, golden vectors and property-based tests.
rationale: This is the product's reason to exist and its single largest correctness risk. A user forgives an ugly screen; they do not forgive money that vanishes. The engine is therefore built with no UI, no database and no clock, so it can be tested to exhaustion.
entry_criteria: docs/ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md approved, with worked examples verified arithmetically.
Domain entities, the Money type and repository interfaces exist from Stage 4.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_5_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 5.1 Engine contracts and the purity harness

5.4 Phase B: worklist, redirects and termination

substages.name: Engine contracts and the purity harness
substages.goal: Implement the request and result types, the failure taxonomy, and a static check proving the engine is pure.
substages.why_it_matters: A pure function needs its whole world passed in. Anything it reaches out for destroys determinism and testability.
entry_criteria: docs/ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md approved, with worked examples verified arithmetically.
Domain entities, the Money type and repository interfaces exist from Stage 4.

work.action: Implement AllocationRequest as an immutable type containing everything the engine needs.
details: income_amount_minor, evaluated_at_ms, rule version snapshot with group and category basis points.
A snapshot per active category: id, group, type, sort_order, ceiling or bill amount, current balance, allocated in current period, redirect target id, is_sink.
sink_category_id, optional overrides map, and the period definition for fixed-recurring categories.
Every field the algorithm document names must be present; a missing field means the engine will be tempted to fetch it.

work.action: Implement AllocationResult as an immutable type.
details: Ordered line items: category_id, amount_minor, reason, redirected_from_category_id, hop_count.
A diagnostics trace: ordered, human-readable events describing every acceptance and redirect.
The rule version id used, and a summary of total allocated, total redirected and categories filled.

work.action: Implement the sealed failure type covering every case in the algorithm document's error taxonomy.
details: IncomeNotPositive, IncomeExceedsMaximum, GroupBasisPointsInvalid, CategoryBasisPointsInvalid, EmptyGroupWithNonZeroShare, SinkMissing, SinkIsCapped, OverridesExceedIncome, OverrideNegative, NoCategoriesAvailableForRemainder.
Each failure carries enough context for the UI to write a specific message - the offending group or category, and the offending value.

work.action: Define the public entry point as a synchronous pure function returning a result-or-failure type.
details: No async, no Future, no callback, no stream.

work.action: Add the static purity check to CI.
details: The engine module imports nothing from Flutter, dart:io, the data layer, or any package that performs I/O.
Demonstrate the check failing on a deliberate import, then revert.

work.action: Implement input validation at the entry point, returning the appropriate typed failure before any computation begins.

acceptance_criteria: The entry point is synchronous and pure, with no async in its signature or body.
The static purity check passes and has been demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation.
Every error case in the algorithm document has a corresponding failure variant carrying diagnostic context.
No AllocationRequest field is missing relative to the algorithm document.
must_not: Do not give the engine a repository, a clock or a logger.
Do not return a bare boolean or null for failure.
common_pitfalls: A convenience overload that fetches balances for the caller, which reintroduces I/O.
Failures without context, so the UI can only say something went wrong.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Phase A: base split and largest-remainder rounding
substages.goal: Implement the integer-only percentage split with deterministic largest-remainder rounding.
substages.why_it_matters: This is where rounding drift is born in almost every budgeting app.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.1 (Engine contracts and the purity harness) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the integer split primitive: given an amount and a list of basis-point weights, return integer shares that sum exactly to the amount.
details: floor_share = (amount * bp) integer-divided by 10000.
remainder_numerator = (amount * bp) modulo 10000.
leftover = amount minus the sum of floors.
Distribute leftover one unit at a time to the largest remainder numerators.

work.action: Implement the deterministic tie-break: lower sort_order first, then lower id by string comparison.
details: Do not rely on the sort being stable; specify both keys explicitly.

work.action: Apply the primitive twice: across groups, then within each group across its categories.
details: Write it once and call it twice; two copies will diverge.

work.action: Implement the overflow guard on the amount times basis points intermediate.
details: Use the documented maximum income from the algorithm document.
Return IncomeExceedsMaximum rather than wrapping.

work.action: Add the phase A conservation assertions inside the engine.
details: Group amounts sum to the income.
Each group's category amounts sum to that group's amount.
These assertions fail loudly; they never adjust a value to make the sum work.

work.action: Write unit tests for the primitive in isolation before testing it through the engine.
details: Equal weights, unequal weights, a single weight of 10000, an amount smaller than the number of weights, an amount of 1, and the tie-break case.
Test with hand-computed expectations, including the V-02 and V-03 cases from the algorithm document.

acceptance_criteria: No floating point operation appears in phase A.
The split primitive returns shares summing exactly to the input for every tested case.
The tie-break is deterministic across repeated runs and across shuffled input order.
An income above the documented maximum returns IncomeExceedsMaximum rather than wrapping.
Conservation assertions fail loudly on a deliberately broken split, demonstrated and reverted.
must_not: Do not distribute leftover units to the first item in iteration order.
Do not write the split logic twice.
common_pitfalls: Relying on map iteration order for determinism.
Computing the remainder as a double to compare fractions.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Headroom computation by category type
substages.goal: Implement how much each category can accept, including the within-run accepted tracker.
substages.why_it_matters: Omitting the within-run tracker is the single most common defect in this algorithm, and it lets a category exceed its ceiling.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.2 (Phase A: base split and largest-remainder rounding) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement headroom for ACCUMULATING_RESERVE: max(0, ceiling minus current balance minus accepted so far this run).
Implement headroom for FIXED_RECURRING: max(0, bill amount minus allocated in current period minus accepted so far this run).
Implement headroom for UNCAPPED_FLOW and for the sink: unbounded.
details: Represent unbounded explicitly rather than as a very large number, so no arithmetic can overflow it.

work.action: Implement the accepted-so-far tracker, scoped to a single allocation run.
details: Two parcels arriving at the same category within one event must not both consume the same headroom.
Write the test for this case before writing the tracker.

work.action: Handle the already-over-ceiling case: a category whose balance already exceeds its ceiling, which can happen after a manual override or a sync merge.
details: Headroom is zero, never negative, and the category redirects everything.

work.action: Write unit tests for headroom in isolation for every type, including zero headroom, full headroom, partially consumed headroom, and the already-over case.

acceptance_criteria: Headroom is never negative for any input.
Two parcels to the same category in one run cannot exceed the combined headroom, proven by a test.
An already-over-ceiling category returns zero headroom and redirects everything.
Unbounded is represented explicitly, not as a magic large number.
must_not: Do not represent unbounded as int64 max, which then overflows when added to.
Do not allow negative headroom to propagate as a negative allocation.
common_pitfalls: Computing headroom once at the start of the run and reusing the stale value for the second parcel.
Forgetting the already-over case, which produces a negative allocation and breaks conservation.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Phase B: worklist, redirects and termination
substages.goal: Implement capacity resolution with chained redirects, cycle defence, hop limit and the terminal sink.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-10 is the app's differentiator, and this is where money either lands somewhere traceable or quietly disappears.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.3 (Headroom computation by category type) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the worklist as an explicit queue rather than recursion.
details: Seed it with the phase A allocations in deterministic order: sort_order then id.
Recursion invites stack overflow on a pathological chain and hides the hop count.

work.action: Implement the parcel: destination category id, pending amount, hop count, visited set, and the category it was redirected from.
Implement the pop-accept-overflow cycle.
details: Compute the destination's current headroom including accepted so far.
accepted = min(pending, headroom); record a line item with its reason.
overflow = pending minus accepted; if greater than zero, push a parcel to the redirect target with hop count incremented and the visited set extended.
Record a diagnostics entry for every acceptance and every redirect.

work.action: Implement cycle defence: if the redirect target is already in the parcel's visited set, route the remainder to the sink with reason SINK_TERMINAL and record a cycle warning.
Implement the hop limit at MAX_HOPS, recommended 32, with the same sink routing and a hop-limit warning.
Implement degraded-target handling: a missing, archived, soft-deleted or self-referencing redirect target routes to the sink with a warning rather than throwing.
Implement the sink-missing case as a typed failure, since it indicates a configuration bug that validation should have caught.
Add the final conservation assertion before returning: the sum of all line items equals the income exactly.
details: On failure, fail loudly with the full diagnostics trace attached. Never adjust a line item to balance the sum.

work.action: Reproduce the reference chained example from the algorithm document as a unit test and confirm every intermediate value matches.

acceptance_criteria: The chained example reproduces exactly: 80,000, 100,000 and 120,000 summing to 300,000.
A configuration containing a redirect cycle terminates and routes the remainder to the sink.
A chain exceeding MAX_HOPS terminates at the sink with a warning.
A degraded redirect target routes to the sink without throwing.
The final conservation assertion fails loudly on a deliberately broken run, demonstrated and reverted.
The diagnostics trace explains every hop in language that could be shown to a user.
must_not: Do not implement chaining with recursion.
Do not clamp and discard overflow.
Do not adjust a line item to satisfy the conservation assertion.
common_pitfalls: A visited set shared across parcels rather than per parcel, which wrongly blocks legitimate multiple arrivals.
Diagnostics written for developers, which then cannot be shown in the Stage 6 preview.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Fixed-recurring period logic
substages.goal: Implement period boundaries and per-period capping for fixed-recurring categories.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-11 - these categories must not accumulate past their bill, and the surplus must go somewhere visible.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.4 (Phase B: worklist, redirects and termination) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement the period boundary calculation from the anchor day, taking the evaluation timestamp from the request rather than a clock.
details: Handle anchor days that do not exist in short months explicitly - an anchor of 31 in February.
Define and implement the rule: clamp to the last day of the month is the conventional choice; state whichever is chosen.

work.action: Take allocated_in_current_period from the request, computed by the data layer, rather than deriving it inside the engine.
Apply the carry-forward or redirect-surplus policy from OQ-05 as an explicit input rather than a hardcoded constant.
details: The policy must be visible in the request so a future change does not require an engine change.

work.action: Handle a bill amount changed mid-period deterministically, and document the behaviour.
Write tests for the period edge cases.
details: Anchor 31 rolling through February in a common year and a leap year.
Anchor 1, the simple case.
A category already fully funded for the period, which accepts nothing and redirects everything.
A category partially funded, which accepts exactly its remaining headroom.
A period boundary crossed between two income events.

acceptance_criteria: An anchor day of 31 rolls through a 28-day February without skipping or duplicating a period, proven by a test.
A fully funded fixed-recurring category accepts zero and redirects the whole allocation.
The period policy is an input, not a constant.
The engine reads no clock to determine the period.
must_not: Do not read the system clock to determine the current period.
Do not hardcode the carry-forward policy.
common_pitfalls: Month arithmetic that produces 31 February and silently rolls into March.
Deriving allocated-in-period inside the engine, which requires a database and breaks purity.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Manual override handling
substages.goal: Implement per-event overrides with proportional redistribution and exact-total enforcement.
substages.why_it_matters: FR-12 lets the user bend the rules for one payment without corrupting the rules or breaking conservation.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.5 (Fixed-recurring period logic) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement override application: overridden categories take their stated amounts, replacing their phase A share.
Implement redistribution of the remainder across non-overridden categories by their relative basis points.
details: Reuse the split primitive from substage 5.2 rather than writing a second rounding path.
Verify against the worked example: income 500,000, Medical overridden to 200,000, Emergency 3500bp and Trip 2500bp receive 175,000 and 125,000.

work.action: Implement the override validation rules, each returning its typed failure.
details: Overrides summing to more than the income.
A negative override amount.
Overrides summing to less than the income with no non-overridden category available.
An override naming a category absent from the request.

work.action: Implement the ceiling policy decided in Stage 2.
details: If overrides may exceed a ceiling, mark the line item MANUAL_OVERRIDE, add a diagnostics warning, and do not redirect it away.
The resulting balance may exceed the ceiling; substage 5.3 already handles the subsequent already-over case.

work.action: Confirm by test that applying an override never mutates the rule version in the request.
Confirm by test that conservation still holds exactly after any override combination.

acceptance_criteria: The worked override example reproduces exactly: 200,000, 175,000 and 125,000 totalling 500,000.
Every override validation rule returns its specific typed failure, each proven by a test.
Overrides summing exactly to the income are accepted with no redistribution.
Conservation holds after every tested override combination.
The rule version snapshot is unmodified after an override, proven by a test.
must_not: Do not write a second rounding implementation for redistribution.
Do not let an override write to the rule version.
common_pitfalls: Redistributing the remainder evenly instead of by relative weight.
Allowing a zero override to be treated as absent rather than as an explicit zero.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Reversal generation
substages.goal: Implement compensating entries that exactly undo a previous income event without touching history.
substages.why_it_matters: OQ-09 and INV-03 - a mis-entered salary must be undoable, and history must remain honest about what happened.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.6 (Manual override handling) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Implement reversal as a mirror of the recorded allocations, with opposing direction, not as a recomputation.
details: State and test why: a rule change between the event and the reversal would otherwise produce a mismatch.

work.action: Ensure each reversal entry references the entry it reverses.
Ensure the reversal is itself conserving: the sum of compensating entries equals the negative of the original event total.
Implement guards: an event cannot be reversed twice, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed.
Write the critical test: change the distribution rules between the event and its reversal, then assert every affected balance returns exactly to its pre-event value.
Write a test asserting no original ledger entry was modified or removed by the reversal.

acceptance_criteria: Reversing an event returns every affected category balance to its pre-event value exactly.
The rule-changed-in-between test passes.
Double reversal is rejected.
No original entry is modified or removed, proven by comparing row contents before and after.
must_not: Do not recompute the allocation on reversal.
Do not delete or edit the original entries.
common_pitfalls: Reversal implemented as re-running the engine with a negative amount, which fails whenever ceilings were involved.
Missing the double-reversal guard, which silently doubles the correction.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Golden test vectors
substages.goal: Implement all fifteen vectors from the design as JSON fixtures with an automatic loader.
substages.why_it_matters: Golden vectors are the regression net that keeps every future refactor honest.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.7 (Reversal generation) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Store each vector as a JSON fixture under test/fixtures/allocation/, using the format defined in Stage 2.
details: Fields: id, description, request, expected_allocations, expected_failure, notes.

work.action: Confirm the loader picks up a new fixture with no code change.
Implement every vector V-01 to V-15 from the design table.
details: V-01 plain three-group split. V-02 largest-remainder rounding. V-03 rounding tie-break.
V-04 single ceiling redirect. V-05 chained multi-hop redirect. V-06 everything full to sink.
V-07 redirect cycle defended. V-08 fixed-recurring overflow. V-09 override with redistribution.
V-10 override exceeding income rejected. V-11 zero and negative income rejected.
V-12 group with share but no categories. V-13 income of one minor unit.
V-14 simultaneous ceiling hits to one target. V-15 very large income across 40 categories.

work.action: For each vector assert both the per-category amounts and the conservation total.
Confirm every expected value came from the design document or an independent hand calculation, never from the implementation's output.
details: If a vector fails, first determine whether the implementation or the expectation is wrong - do not default to trusting the code.

work.action: Add each worked example from the algorithm document as a vector if it is not already covered.

acceptance_criteria: All fifteen vectors pass.
Adding a new JSON fixture is picked up automatically with no code change.
Every expected value is traceable to the design document or a recorded hand calculation.
Each vector asserts conservation in addition to per-category amounts.
must_not: Do not generate expected values from the implementation.
Do not skip a vector because it is inconvenient.
common_pitfalls: Fixing a failing vector by editing the expectation, which enshrines the bug.
A fixture format that cannot express an expected failure, so the rejection cases get omitted.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Record evidence in docs/reports/STAGE_5_WORKLOG.md, then continue to substage 5.9. Do not skip ahead or work substages in parallel.
escalate_immediately_if: A vector fails and the design document appears to be wrong - stop and raise it rather than editing either side.

substages.name: Property-based tests
substages.goal: Verify the seven required properties over thousands of randomly generated configurations.
substages.why_it_matters: Hand-picked examples find the bugs you imagined. Properties find the ones you did not.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.8 (Golden test vectors) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Build the generator for randomised configurations.
details: 1 to 60 categories across three groups.
Random valid basis-point splits that total exactly 10000 at each level.
Random ceilings and balances, including already-over-ceiling states.
Random redirect graphs, including adversarial ones with long chains and deliberate cycles.
Random category types, including fixed-recurring with random period states.
Always a valid uncapped sink.

work.action: Build the income generator from 1 up to the documented maximum, weighted to include small awkward values.
Implement the seven properties.
details: P1 conservation: the sum of allocations equals the income exactly.
P2 non-negativity: no allocation is negative.
P3 ceiling respect: no accumulating category ends above its ceiling unless a manual override caused it and the line item is marked accordingly.
P4 determinism: running the same case twice produces identical output including ordering.
P5 termination: every case completes within the hop limit, with no stack overflow.
P6 input-order independence: shuffling the category order in the request does not change the result.
P7 scaling: with no ceilings in play, doubling the income changes each allocation by its doubled share within at most one minor unit.

work.action: Run at least a few thousand cases in CI and record the seed so any failure is reproducible.
Shrink every failing case to a minimal reproduction and add it permanently to the golden vectors.
details: A property failure that is fixed without a permanent vector will come back.

work.action: Record the case count and the seed in the stage report.

acceptance_criteria: All seven properties hold over at least several thousand generated cases.
The seed is recorded and a failing run is reproducible from it.
Every discovered failure has been added to test/fixtures/allocation/ as a permanent vector.
The generator produces adversarial redirect graphs including cycles, verified by inspecting a sample.
outputs: New golden vectors from shrunk failures.
must_not: Do not weaken a property to make it pass.
Do not fix a property failure without adding a permanent vector.
common_pitfalls: A generator that never produces the interesting cases, so the properties always pass vacuously.
Property tests excluded from CI because they are slow, which is where they stop finding anything.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Benchmarks, engine notes and gate preparation
substages.goal: Measure engine performance, document the implementation, and prepare the stage gate.
substages.why_it_matters: NFR-06 - the allocation preview recomputes as the user types, so it must be fast on a modest phone.
entry_criteria: Substage 5.9 (Property-based tests) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Benchmark allocation across 10, 40 and 100 categories, with and without redirect chains.
details: Record median and worst case, and name the device or machine used.
Include a pathological case: 100 categories all at their ceilings, chaining to the sink.

work.action: If a target is missed, profile before optimising, and never trade correctness for speed.
details: Any optimisation must leave every vector and property passing unchanged.

work.action: Audit engine coverage to at least 95 percent line and branch, naming and justifying every uncovered branch.
Write docs/ENGINE_NOTES.md.
details: Implementation notes and the public API.
Every deviation from ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md, with the algorithm document amended to match reality.
Benchmark results with the device named.
The documented maximum income and other known limitations.
The guarantees Stage 6 may rely on.

work.action: Re-run the full suite from a clean checkout and capture the output.
Update docs/TRACEABILITY.md for the requirements this stage completes.
Write docs/reports/STAGE_5_REPORT.md and prepare the gate question with concrete figures.

acceptance_criteria: Allocation across 100 categories completes within the NFR-06 budget of 50ms, with the figure recorded.
The pathological all-ceilings case is benchmarked and recorded.
Engine coverage is at least 95 percent line and branch.
ENGINE_NOTES.md records every deviation and the algorithm document has been amended to match.
The full suite passes from a clean checkout.
must_not: Do not optimise before profiling.
Do not leave a deviation undocumented.
common_pitfalls: Benchmarking on a development machine and reporting it as phone performance.
Coverage reached by tests that exercise lines without asserting behaviour.

stage_definition_of_done: Every golden vector V-01 to V-15 passes.
All seven properties P1 to P7 hold over thousands of generated cases.
Engine line and branch coverage is at least 95 percent, with every uncovered branch named and justified.
The engine has no dependency on Flutter, the database, the network or the system clock, proven by a static check.
Any deviation from ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md is documented and the algorithm document is amended to match reality.
stage_must_not: Do not wire the engine into any UI until every test passes.
Do not use floating point anywhere, including in tests, fixtures and benchmarks.
Do not silently correct a conservation failure by adjusting the last allocation - assert and fail.
Do not let the engine read the clock, the database or any global state.
Do not implement ceiling logic that clamps and discards excess.
Do not change the algorithm design here without amending docs/ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md and raising it.
anti_patterns: Computing shares with doubles and rounding at the end, producing off-by-one drift for certain amounts.
Recursion for redirect chains without a depth guard.
Copying the implementation's output into a test's expected values.
Treating a failed conservation assertion as a rounding nuisance to be smoothed over.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: The pure entry point is what the Add Income preview calls on every keystroke in Stage 6.
The diagnostics trace is what the preview renders to explain redirects.
Typed failures map directly to Stage 6 error messages.
Reversal generation backs the undo feature in Stage 6.
handoff.summary_to_write: State the engine's public API, its documented maximum income, and the guarantees the UI may rely on.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 5 (Distribution engine) is complete. All <N> golden vectors and <M> property-based cases pass; coverage is <X> percent; worst-case allocation across 100 categories is <T>ms. Do you approve moving to Stage 6, the UI?
